task.title: Find and fix the mistakes in a sales sheet
task.brief: Your manager shared a small sales sheet (below) and says the totals look wrong. Take about 15 minutes. Write: (1) each mistake you find, with the cell; (2) the correct formula or fix for it; (3) the correct grand total; and (4) a 2–3 line note to your manager saying what you fixed. Plain words are fine. A good answer finds most of the mistakes and gives formulas that would work when copied down.
task.material:
Sheet: October sales (GST is 18% on every row)
Row 1 headers: A Invoice | B Customer | C City | D Amount (₹) | E GST | F Total
Row 2: INV-101 | Kiran Stores | Pune | 12,000 | =D2*18 | =D2+E2
Row 3: INV-102 | Noor Traders | Nagpur | 8,500 | =D3*18% | =D3+E3
Row 4: INV-103 | Arul Agencies | Chennai | 15,000 | =D4*18% | =D4+E4
Row 5: INV-104 | Mehta & Co | Surat | '20,000 (left-aligned, green triangle) | =D5*18% | =D5+E5
Row 6: INV-105 | Das Electricals | Kolkata | 5,500 | =D6*18% | =D5+E5
Row 8: Grand total | | | =SUM(D2:D5) | | =SUM(F2:F6)
Commission rate is typed in H1 = 2%.
Row 2 commission: G2 = D2*H1, then copied down to G6 (G3 to G6 now show 0).
Rate lookup: I2 = VLOOKUP(C2, Rates!A:B, 2, TRUE)
key_points: E2 multiplies by 18 instead of 18%: should be =D2*18%
D5 is a number stored as text, so SUM skips it: convert it to a number
F6 points to row 5: should be =D6+E6
D8 total leaves out row 6: should be =SUM(D2:D6)
VLOOKUP should use FALSE for an exact match
Correct amount total is ₹61,000 (₹71,980 with GST)
A short, clear note to the manager listing the fixes

rubric.label: Correct fixes
rubric.guide: 0 = no real mistakes found, 3 = about half found with working fixes, 5 = nearly all found and every fix works

rubric.label: Completeness
rubric.guide: 0 = one or two lines only, 3 = mistakes listed but no total or note, 5 = mistakes, fixes, correct total and note all given

rubric.label: Clarity
rubric.guide: 0 = hard to follow, 3 = understandable but messy, 5 = each mistake, cell and fix is clear and easy to check

rubric.label: Note to manager
rubric.guide: 0 = no note or rude, 3 = note is there but vague, 5 = short, polite note that says what changed
